subject: Partner roster and geo-justification request for EU customers
messages:
From: Megan Holt <megan.holt@cloudstream.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 May 2029 13:12:00 +0100
Subject: Request: full partner roster + geo-justification for EU customers

Hi Aditya,

Per the data protection checklist for our upcoming EU pilot, our privacy team has asked for a current list of all third-party partners (subprocessors) CloudStream uses to process customer data on your behalf, with the following fields: name, processing role (e.g., telemetry, hosting, analytics), primary processing country, whether the subprocessors have EU onshore options, and whether transfers rely on SCCs or other safeguards.

Can you provide that roster plus any short justification notes for partners that route data outside the EU (for example, where an onshore fallback is not available)? We need this to complete our DPA Annex review and produce the customer-facing exportability statement. If you can share a CSV with the columns above and any supporting data flow diagram, that would be ideal.

We also need to confirm whether any of your telemetry/observability vendors retain logs outside the EU for longer than 90 days — call that out explicitly.

Target timeline from our side is 48 hours if possible; legal is waiting for the packet. Happy to hop on a quick call if it helps.

Thanks,

Megan Holt
Head of Security & Privacy
CloudStream Solutions
megan.holt@cloudstream.com
+44 20 7946 0XXX

Attachment: none (initial request)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 20 May 2029 15:45:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Request: full partner roster + geo-justification for EU customers

Hi Megan — thanks for the clear checklist. We're on it.

Quick notes:
- I'll coordinate with Security and Legal for the export packet. Kim, Lauren — looping you in to confirm the retention callouts and DPA excerpt.
- We can provide a CSV and a high-level data flow diagram. We do have a small set of telemetry partners that default to US-hosted endpoints but offer EU residency options for enterprise customers; we'll flag those and provide the justification for why the default path exists and how onshore fallbacks work.
- Will call out any vendor retention windows >90d as requested.

Can you confirm whether you need signed attestation (DPA addendum) or a plain roster for now? I ask because if Legal needs an amendment we may need additional signatures and that changes timelines.

I should have a first-pass packet for you by tomorrow EOD CET. If that's tight, we can set up a 30-min sync this afternoon.

Best,
Aditya Rao

Subject: INTERNAL: CloudStream roster request — ask Legal and Security for narrow deliverables

Kim / Lauren — quick internal note before I send the packet:

1) Deliverables we should produce to CloudStream:
   - CSV: name | role | primary processing country | EU onshore available (Y/N) | safeguards (SCCs / BCRs / other) | retention window days | notes
   - One-page dataflow (PDF) that highlights where EU personal data may cross borders and which partners have onshore fallbacks
   - DPA excerpt: the current Subprocessor Annex language we offer (attach a short snippet)

2) Likely items to flag upfront:
   - Observability vendor "StreamSight" has default US ingestion but EU region available for enterprise customers; retention default 120d (we can show how to reduce to 30d for EU accounts)
   - Aggregation analytics partner "MetricWave" processes anonymized telemetry in the EU but uses a US ML pipeline for model training; will need to explain pseudonymization steps

3) Timeline: propose sending draft roster to CloudStream by tomorrow 10:00 CET; final packet by tomorrow EOD (we may need a 24h extension for signed addendum).

If you want to change language in the DPA excerpt I'll let Legal propose the final snippet — we should avoid promises on modifying retention programmatically unless Product signs off.

-Aditya

From: Megan Holt <megan.holt@cloudstream.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Cc: Carlos Benitez <c.benitez@cloudstream.com>, Legal Team <legal@cloudstream.com>
Date: Tue, 21 May 2029 09:30:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Request: full partner roster + geo-justification for EU customers

Aditya — appreciate the quick turnaround. Attached is the roster and a short diagram; CC'd Legal and Carlos (compliance lead) for completeness.

Highlights from the attached packet:
- Attached CSV (cloudstream_subprocessors_20290521.csv) lists 18 subprocessors; three partners are marked as "default: US" with EU onshore options (StreamSight, MetricWave, CacheBridge). For each we included the region of processing and the contractual safeguard (SCCs).
- Data flow PDF (cloudstream_eu_dataflow_v1.pdf) shows which flows are encrypted in transit and where onshore fallbacks exist.
- DPA excerpt (dpa-excerpt-subprocessors.docx) includes the clause we use to request notification and a 30-day review period for subprocessor changes.

Please confirm receipt and we can set a short call if you'd like us to walk through specific rows. We're happy to add additional evidence (SOC reports) for any vendor if that helps speed internal sign-off.

Files attached: cloudstream_subprocessors_20290521.csv (CSV), cloudstream_eu_dataflow_v1.pdf (PDF), dpa-excerpt-subprocessors.docx (DOCX)

Best,
Megan Holt
Head of Security & Privacy
CloudStream Solutions
